checkpoints.name: Maryland
checkpoints.cite: docs/research/2026-11-16-numbers-and-facts-1861.md, Priority 1 sides table: Union, not seceded, Hicks governor, Federal troops at Baltimore from 13 May (MSA exhibit; OR I-2 p. 29)

checkpoints.name: Delaware
checkpoints.cite: docs/research/2026-11-16-numbers-and-facts-1861.md, Priority 1 sides table: Union, not seceded, Burton governor (AAC)

checkpoints.name: Kentucky
checkpoints.cite: docs/research/2026-11-16-numbers-and-facts-1861.md, Priority 1 sides table: neutral by the Governor's proclamation of 20 May, government not seceded (AAC; Kentucky archives)

checkpoints.name: Missouri

docs/research/2026-11-16-numbers-and-facts-1861.md, Priority 1 'Whether Washington is held': yes, throughout; isolated 19 to 25 April, never attacked (OR I-2 pp. 29 to 30, 38 to 40, 314 to 316)

docs/research/2026-11-16-numbers-and-facts-1861.md, Priority 1 'Each side's men under arms': a block's strength is men present, which lies between present for duty (inferred about 100,000 to 165,000) and the rolls (inferred about 145,000 to 245,000); the edges rounded outward per the review nit (95,000; 250,000). No dated 31 July return exists: the note's rule is that a run is not failed below the lower edge

docs/research/2026-11-16-numbers-and-facts-1861.md, Priority 1 and Appendix B A3: whole Confederacy about 112,040 in July (Livermore p. 42, an estimate he calls probably too low), rounded outward to 100,000; above 32,232 effectives at Bull Run alone (Livermore p. 77). No sourced upper bound: the lead sets it once Walker's or Cooper's returns (OR IV-1) are read

docs/research/2026-11-16-numbers-and-facts-1861.md, Priority 1 'Planned operations fought' and Appendix B B2: at least the one Livermore-scale case (McDowell's offensive, First Bull Run); at most the 26 cases of B1, every battle and planned skirmish read. A count of the record's cases, never a required event

docs/research/2026-11-16-numbers-and-facts-1861.md, Priority 1 and Appendix B B2: the Confederate side planned almost nothing in the window (Sumter, Cole Camp inferred, Mesilla; Carthage disputed), so the count does not require one; at most those four

victory.cite: [I] proposed by lane 1.14 (notes/lane-1.14-done-check.md), for the lead to rule: read from the checkpoint scores; a capital weighs 1000, twice the most the men share can give (500 permille above an even split, at 1 a permille); a government a tenth of a capital; men and ground 1 a permille each
